title: Panorama merges and the merge preview
objective: Open a merge preview first for HDR and panoramas, and turn a selection of overlapping RAW or JPEG frames into one durable, editable panorama in Select, with one Merge panorama action, a result-led stack, the HDR lifecycle, Boundary Warp and derived sources up to 512 MP, through the shared command service.
context_summary: Scope: a merge preview that opens first for both kinds; RAW or JPEG frames (never mixed), from a selection or a panorama Select groups; automatic crop with Boundary Warp; and derived-source limits raised to 65,000 pixels a side and 512 MP. HDR merges are delivered, and this plan generalizes their boundary and reuses their storage, lifecycle, stacks and catalog folder choice. TASK-001 to TASK-011 are complete: the kind-tagged boundary, HDR's merge preview, paged derived storage and preparation, the banded reference, GPU editing and export of paged sources, merge frame development, rotating-camera registration, the stitch, the job and commands, Select's panorama menu, sheet and stack, and the background `panorama-merge` journey, which passes in the rendered tier on the M4. TASK-012 remains: the rendered evidence still unrun or short (the hdr-merge journey through the preview, the derived-paged GPU corpus entry's remaining cells and gaps), natural-panorama quality and photo-sized measurement. No HDR panoramas, edge fill, manual control points, compatibility shims or approval/research task. Recorded defaults (2–32 frames, projections, Boundary Warp 0, the bracket refusals, a baked lens profile, a usage-statistics exemption) are in the design and decisions.

tasks.description: Stitch registered frames: projection, photometric fit, seams, band-limited blending and Boundary Warp, chunk by chunk.

Perspective, Cylindrical, Spherical and Auto projections with `ExcessiveFieldOfView`; output scale at the reference's centre, never upscaled, scaled down uniformly past the large-source limits (`OutputTooLarge` only where even that cannot fit).

Per-frame gains (one a channel for JPEG, one a frame for RAW) from overlapping unclipped samples; seams by a minimum-cost cut on the proxies; a band-limited blend whose widest band is bounded so each output chunk reads bounded windows.

Boundary Warp 0–100: crop to the largest covered rectangle at 0, a content-preserving mesh warp onto the bounding rectangle at 100, scaled displacements between; the warp is part of the one output mapping, so frames are resampled once; `InsufficientCoverage` below a quarter of the rectangle a side.
Diagnostics as the design lists; output bit-identical for any split into chunks.

extra_context: Minimum implementation model: roadmap high tier or stronger. Re-review the design and current main, and look for a branch or worktree already carrying this task, before starting. Numerical, solver, backend and layout details are delegated within the design; do not add a product-review or research gate. A test filter named here must run the tests this task adds; an empty filtered run is not evidence. Run quick once at the task's handoff; rendered and timing runs follow the project's verification rules.

Rendered evidence first: run the hdr-merge journey, whose Merge HDR and preview steps have not been run, and the derived-paged GPU corpus entry's remaining cells and gaps: crop-straightened a pixel short of the reference below 100%, detail-presence-masked's tiles at 100% not drawn, and its histogram, minimap overview and resized, 16-bit and sharpened exports. Fix each miss or record it as a limit in the GPU-first design; measure after the fixes.

Natural panoramas: the owner's own where available (Z6, X100VI, Air 2S) and pinned open samples otherwise; inspect seams, levelling, colour, crop losses and warp quality; record scope honestly and fix measured failures. Missing private inputs leave quality unqualified, never block measurement.

Measure once behind the host lock: stages cold and warm, cancellation, temporary disk, peak process/source/scratch/GPU use, editor latency at Fit and 100% on a 512 MP result, export time and browse latency beside a merge, for 24 and 60 MP frames, 5 and 32 of them; and HDR 60 MP × 9 fusion with band reads out of the file cache.

acceptance_criteria: The hdr-merge journey passes through the preview; the derived-paged entry passes the GPU gate within its declared tolerances, or each remaining miss is recorded as a limit.
Figures and their scope are recorded in the performance spec, the design and feature status; unmeasured cases are named.
Natural-panorama findings are recorded with their sources; measured failures are fixed or recorded as limits.

steps: Run the hdr-merge journey and the GPU gate over the derived sources.
Prepare photo-sized generated workloads and a natural-case manifest.
Measure on the completed feature behind the host lock and inspect natural results.
expected_results: Every stated acceptance check passes with its recorded scope; skipped checks are not passes.
